subject: environmental
audience: FE Environmental candidates and environmental engineering students
title: The Clarifier System That Needed 12,000 ft², Not 6,000
featured_title: THE CLARIFIER SYSTEM THAT NEEDED 12000 SQ FT, NOT 6000

presentation.challenge: Splitting the flow between two clarifiers did not halve the total required area. The system still needed 12,000 ft² in service.

practice.primary_question: How is clarifier surface area sized from flow rate and surface overflow rate?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Sizing one of two parallel clarifiers for half the flow and then incorrectly reporting that single-basin area as the total required system area.

case_dna.target_misconception: If two clarifiers split the flow equally, the total surface area requirement is half the single-system requirement.
case_dna.why_plausible: Each clarifier handles half the flow, so the area of each unit is half, but the two unit areas must still be added.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: At Q=6.0 MGD and allowable overflow rate 500 gpd/ft², total area is 6,000,000/500=12,000 ft². Two equal basins require 6,000 ft² each, not 6,000 ft² total.
case_dna.corrected_model: Surface overflow rate is Q/A. Parallel basins divide both the flow and the required area among units; total active area remains Q divided by the design overflow rate.

problem_statement: A sedimentation system must treat 6.0 MGD at a design surface overflow rate of 500 gpd/ft². Two identical clarifiers will operate in parallel and split the flow equally. A design note sizes one clarifier at 6,000 ft² and mistakenly reports 6,000 ft² as the total area. Determine the required total surface area and the area of each clarifier.

gates.heading: The per-basin area was mistaken for total system area.
gates.prompt: What stays fixed when the flow is split equally between identical units?
gates.cta: Preserve Q/A for each active unit

gates.label: Theory
gates.heading: Choose the correct clarifier sizing relation

options.label: Use A_total=Q_total/SOR
options.reason: Surface overflow rate is defined as flow divided by plan area.

options.label: Use A_total=(Q_total/2)/SOR and stop there
options.reason: That computes the area of one clarifier, not the total area of two clarifiers.

options.label: Use A_total=Q_total×SOR
options.reason: That is dimensionally inconsistent with Q/A=SOR.

gates.heading: Predict the total active clarifier area
gates.prompt: Enter the total area in ft².

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Apply the design overflow rate
gates.result: The two clarifiers require 12,000 ft² of total active surface area.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the required area
gates.success: Total active area is 12,000 ft², so each of two equal clarifiers is 6,000 ft².
gates.hint: Convert 6.0 MGD to 6,000,000 gpd before dividing by the overflow rate.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Parallelization divides the area, not the total requirement

cards.text: Each basin receives 3.0 MGD and needs 3,000,000/500=6,000 ft².
Two 6,000 ft² basins provide the required 12,000 ft² total active area.

gates.heading: Correct the clarifier-sizing note
report: C1. The total plant flow is 6.0 MGD.
C2. Two clarifiers split the flow equally.
C3. One clarifier needs 6,000 ft², so the total required area is 6,000 ft².

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: This is the stated total flow.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated operating arrangement.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It reports a single-unit area as the combined system area.

evidence_choices.label: 2×6000=12,000 ft² total
evidence_choices.reason: Both parallel clarifiers contribute active settling area.

correction.template: The system requires {total_area} ft² total, with {each_area} ft² per clarifier.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Check the system if one clarifier is out of service
gates.constraint: Keep total plant flow at 6.0 MGD with only one 6,000 ft² clarifier operating.

options.label: Overflow rate remains 500 gpd/ft²
options.reason: The active area is halved while full flow remains.

options.label: Overflow rate falls to 250 gpd/ft²
options.reason: Losing area increases Q/A rather than decreasing it.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Size a different clarifier system
gates.prompt: What total area is required for 4.0 MGD at 800 gpd/ft²?

options.label: 8,000 ft²
options.reason: That would correspond to a lower overflow rate.

gates.explanation: Clarifier plan area follows A=Q/SOR for the specified design condition.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the clarifier sizing
gates.confirmation: I confirm that the total required clarifier surface area is based on total flow and design overflow rate, even when the area is divided among parallel units.

items.label: What failed
items.value: A per-unit clarifier area was mistaken for total installed active area.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: Both parallel basins contribute to the total plan area.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use A_total=Q_total/SOR, then divide that area among equal parallel basins.

seo.seo_title: Clarifier Surface Overflow Rate and Area | FE Environmental E-072
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Environmental Case E-072: 6.0 MGD at 500 gpd/ft² requires 12,000 ft² total clarifier area, or 6,000 ft² per basin for two units.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Environmental clarifier surface overflow rate
seo.excerpt: Splitting flow between parallel clarifiers does not reduce the total surface area required at the same design overflow rate.
seo.direct_answer: Surface overflow rate is Q/A. For 6.0 MGD at 500 gpd/ft², total required area is 6,000,000/500=12,000 ft². With two equal parallel clarifiers, each basin requires 6,000 ft².

faqs.q: How do you calculate clarifier surface area from overflow rate?
faqs.a: Use A=Q/SOR with consistent flow and area units.

faqs.q: What happens to overflow rate if one of two equal clarifiers goes offline at full plant flow?
faqs.a: It doubles because the active area is cut in half.
